A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same temporal graph generation method and OmniTemp dataset. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original GPT-4o and supervised-model experiments across four datasets, annotation-quality measurements, and analyses of accuracy, consistency, efficiency and annotation coverage.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds DeepSeek-R1 experiments, additional-model evaluations and generation-count sensitivity results. Some supervised F1 entries are attributed to prior work, but substantial original results remain.

M1.justification: Both versions use timeline-first prompting, DOT graph output, five generations, label-distribution aggregation and the same referenced ILP consistency optimizer. V2 reorganizes these components and shortens method names; its additional backbone evaluations and formal details do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate temporal relation extraction on MATRES, TB-Dense, NT-6 and OmniTemp, including the same sentence-distance subsets. OmniTemp's population and annotation coverage remain unchanged, as do NT-6's overlap exclusion and 18-event evaluation sampling. Additional LLM configurations introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes Bayesian + Constraints scores for MATRES and TB-Dense while retaining that comparator on NT-6 and OmniTemp. Sentence-distance comparisons add SelfConsistency and GlobalConsistency, whereas efficiency comparisons narrow from five zero-shot methods to CoT versus GlobalConsistency. The principal baseline families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands experimental configurations with DeepSeek-R1 and additional o3-mini, LLaMA and Gemini tests. Efficiency evaluation extends across all four test sets and two backbones, with costs estimated from token counts and official prices instead of OpenAI billing. MATRES/TB-Dense supervised F1 comparisons switch from reproduced runs to published scores.

E4.justification: V2 extends component, event-count and relation-type analyses to DeepSeek-R1, includes consistency variants in sentence-distance analyses, and supplies a 1–6-generation sensitivity curve supporting the existing five-generation choice (Figure 5). The original annotation-inconsistency and transitive-closure analyses remain; the new ablation section also reorganizes previously evaluated variants.

E5.justification: V1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5 retain identical GPT-4o means and standard deviations over five generations. Both describe single evaluations for CoT and the consistency variants. V2 adds no new confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation practice; its generation-count curve studies ensemble size.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive DeepSeek-R1, consistency, efficiency and additional-model results. In Table 2, GPT-4o SelfConsistency changes from 58.0 to 60.1 on MATRES and 72.4 to 71.0 on OmniTemp; GlobalConsistency on OmniTemp changes from 74.5 to 73.6. OmniTemp CoT inconsistencies change from 29 to 374 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 2), without explaining the revision. Supervised F1 changes partly reflect replacement with published scores.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix G adds binary decision variables, an explicit ILP objective, and mathematical uniqueness, symmetry and transitivity constraints. V1 Appendix F provides distribution averaging and a brief optimizer description. This expands the formal specification of the retained optimizer without introducing a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain efficient, globally consistent zero-shot temporal graph generation, competitive performance with supervised models, and complete annotation of selected events in OmniTemp. V2 foregrounds existing evaluation-bias analyses and adds supporting model evidence without materially redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the event-count hypothesis with DeepSeek-R1's resilience on MATRES and discusses accuracy–cost tradeoffs when CoT wins on sparse datasets. Appendix B replaces expectations of similar performance across LLMs with evidence of model dependence. V2 also removes the explicit limitation that OmniTemp's start-time-only schema does not cover duration/end-time TRE tasks.

D1.justification: V2 adds API details for additional LLMs, an approximately $400 experimental cost, development-set tuning information, and more explicit TI computation details. It clarifies gold-only CoT accuracy evaluation versus all-pair efficiency evaluation and links the EventFull guidelines repository. Existing training hardware, epochs, segmentation details and planned OmniTemp release are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Brown et al. (2020), Wei et al. (2022), Jain et al. (2023) and Ning et al. (2024), while removing Wen and Ji (2021) and Zhou et al. (2022). These modestly expand the LLM-capability motivation while retaining the principal research positioning. EventFull's 2024-to-2025 citation is a publication update to the same work.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction and method narrative, replacing the staged method progression with Prompt Structure and Post Process subsections and a separate ablation-design section. Annotation details move to Appendix E, qualitative analysis becomes Discussion, and results and limitations are extensively edited.

P2.justification: Table 2 becomes a full-width F1/TI comparison with separate backbone blocks. The original combined efficiency table is replaced by separate cost and time tables. Event-count and distance plots gain series, DeepSeek-R1 plots enter the main text, GPT-4o plots move to the appendices, and a generation-count figure is added. Several original appendix illustrations remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation beyond GPT-4o, makes model-dependent accuracy–cost tradeoffs visible, documents generation-count sensitivity, and specifies the optimizer more clearly. These improve the evidence and exposition for the retained method. The net gain is tempered by unexplained revisions to existing F1/TI values, supervised rows combining published F1 with retrained-model TI, and removal of OmniTemp's explicit applicability caveat.
